back: A person who buys or uses goods and services for his or her own use, not to resell.
Measures by government, organisations and consumers to stop consumers being cheated, harmed or treated unfairly.
Short measures, false descriptions, unsafe goods, expired goods, overpricing, misleading adverts, counterfeits, unfair credit (any five).
Safety, information, choice, being heard, redress, consumer education, basic needs, healthy environment (any six).
The right to a fair settlement of genuine complaints: repair, replacement, refund or compensation.
Unequal knowledge and power, misleading advertising, unsafe goods, vulnerable consumers, complex contracts.
Check goods and dates; compare prices; read labels and contracts; keep receipts; complain properly; report offences (any four).

front: How does consumer protection help honest businesses?
back: It stops dishonest rivals cheating customers and builds trust, so consumers buy with confidence.
